newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil power privatization needed - BNDES.
newsitem.headline: Brazil power privatization needed - BNDES.

text.p: Economists at Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) said privatization in the power sector had to be pushed forward in order to avoid a possible energy crisis in the next few years.

In its November Economic Synopsis the BNDES said 20.3 billion reais ($19.52 billion) would have to be invested in the power sector over the next four years, assuming an average economic growth rate of five percent and an average increase in energy demand of 4.9 percent. An even greater rise in power consumption would require even larger investments in order to stave off a lack of power supply.
"Given that the state-owned power companies do not have the means to finance investments of that size, private sector investment has become crucial," the BNDES said.
"Therefore it is important to push ahead with the privatization process, to create new means of financing (these long-term investments) and draw up rules for new players entering the power sector."

Between 1981 and 1996 energy consumption in Brazil has increased at a faster rate than economic growth. Existing electricity plants are working at full capacity and low rainfalls in the past two years have aggravated the possibility of a power deficit.
In the first eight months of 1996, energy demand has grown six percent in comparison with the same period in 1995, the BNDES said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
